title: आधुनिक नेपाली निबन्धको लाक्षणिक भाषा
nepali: सार पूर्वीय एवम् पाश्चात्य साहित्यशास्त्रमा वर्णित लाक्षणिक भाषाको प्रयोग सम्बन्धी अवधारणालाई स्पष्ट गर्दै स्थापित विविध मान्यताहरू मध्ये मानवीकरण र रूपकीय प्रयोगको उपयोगद्वारा लक्ष्मीप्रसाद देवकोटा, कृष्णचन्द्रसिंह प्रधान, शङ्कर लामिछाने र तारानाथ शर्माका खासखास निबन्धांशमा प्रयुक्त लाक्षणिक अभिव्यक्तिको विश्लेषण यस लेखमा गरिएको छ । सामग्री सङ्कलनका क्रममा उद्देश्यमूलक जनसाङ्खिकी विधिको उपयोग भएको छ भने तथ्य विश्लेषणका क्रममा आवश्यकताअनुसार आगमनात्मक र निगमनात्मक विधिको प्रयोग यस लेखमा भएको छ । चार निबन्धकारका लाक्षणिक अभिव्यक्तिको विश्लेषणका क्रममा प्रयोजनवती लक्षणाका शुद्धा र गौणी लक्षणाको व्यापक रूपमा प्रयोग भएको तथ्य यसमा प्राप्त हुन्छ । त्यसमा पनि शुद्धाका उपादान लक्षणा र गौणीका सारोपा एवम् साध्यवसाना लक्षणा समर्थ ढङ्गले प्रकट भएका छन् । जड एवम् सजीव प्रकृतिको मानवीकृत प्रयोगले उपादान लक्षणाको रचना गरेको छ भने रूपक एवम् रूपकातिसयोक्तिले सारोपा एवम् साध्यवसाना लक्षणालाई मूर्त तुल्याएको भेटिन्छ । नेपाली निबन्धमा प्रयुक्त लाक्षणिक भापाको सर्वाधिक उपलब्धि उपादान लक्षणा हो र गौण उलपब्धि सारोपा तथा साध्यवसाना लक्षणा हुन् ।
american_english: Clarifying the concepts regarding the use of figurative language described in Eastern and Western poetics, this article analyzes figurative expressions employed in specific essay excerpts of Laxmi Prasad Devkota, Krishna Chandra Singh Pradhan, Shankar Lamichhane, and Taranath Sharma through the use of personification and metaphorical application among various established conventions. During data collection, a purposive demographic method was utilized, while during factual analysis, inductive and deductive methods were used in this article as needed. In analyzing the figurative expressions of the four essayists, the fact is obtained herein that shuddha and gauni lakshana of prayojanavati lakshana are extensively used. Even within those, upadana lakshana of shuddha, and saropa along with sadhyavasana lakshana of gauni, are capably manifested. While the personified use of inanimate and animate nature has constructed upadana lakshana, metaphor and metaphorical hyperbole are found to have materialized saropa and sadhyavasana lakshana. The primary achievement of figurative language used in Nepali essays is upadana lakshana, and the secondary achievements are saropa and sadhyavasana lakshana.

informal_english: Clarifying the concepts around using figurative language described in Eastern and Western poetics, this article analyses figurative expressions used in specific essay excerpts of Laxmi Prasad Devkota, Krishna Chandra Singh Pradhan, Shankar Lamichhane, and Taranath Sharma through personification and metaphorical use across various established traditions. During material collection, a purposive demographic method was used, while for factual analysis, inductive and deductive methods were used in this article as needed. Looking at the figurative expressions of the four essayists, it turns out that shuddha and gauni forms of prayojanavati lakshana get heaps of use here. Even within those, the upadana lakshana of shuddha, and the saropa plus sadhyavasana lakshana of gauni, come through pretty strongly. While treating both inanimate and living nature with personification crafts upadana lakshana, metaphor and metaphorical exaggeration make saropa and sadhyavasana lakshana fully concrete. The main takeaway of figurative language used in Nepali essays is upadana lakshana, and the secondary takeaways are saropa and sadhyavasana lakshana.
translator_notes: The opening word 'सार' (Abstract) is treated as an introductory heading prefix and omitted from sentence body. Technical Sanskrit poetics terminology for figurative signification (लक्षणा / lakshana)—specifically प्रयोजनवती लक्षणा (prayojanavati lakshana), शुद्धा (shuddha), गौणी (gauni), उपादान (upadana), सारोपा (saropa), and साध्यवसाना (sadhyavasana)—is transliterated and retained consistently. Source typos 'भापाको' (for भाषाको) and 'उलपब्धि' (for उपलब्धि) translated in context; exact sentence order preserved.
